refutations.target: F7 crash-window threshold ('Reachable only if the BEAR_DEATH clip runs >=95 frames')
refutations.problem: This is not a >= threshold, and 95 is wrong. TTLMAX is 96 and doDying disposes when ttl <= 0. With no red-freeze frames the crash needs a clip of exactly 96 frames. At 95, ttl is still 1 after deathAnimEnd, and doDying disposes safely. At 97 or more, doDying disposes on frame 96, before the clip finishes, and the next update returns at 'mcs == null'. Red-freeze frames during the clip pause ttl but not the clock (redFreeze() does not set animFrozen for DYING), so the general condition is clipFrames minus red-freeze frames = 96.

Because the bear does not override gotHit, it runs the base version, and the base treats a weapon-slot hit as a parry: no damage, no 12-frame invulnerability, no hit sound, and the hit flag is cleared. The wolf, the nearest sibling that fights, has the same jaw-in-weapon-slot layout. It overrides gotHit to do the reverse: a hit there doubles damage and counts as a beheading. So by inheritance the bear is the INVERSE of the wolf. That is a quirk it inherits, not a change the bear makes itself, and it is the same easy-to-miss pattern F8(3) warns about for setLevel. Separately, the head (part 16) and neck (part 12) have real art, so the base's behead flag and x1.5 damage apply to a bear. The port is faithful here (Npc.ts:337-339 returns false on OG_PART.weapon), but only if a future hit-geometry adapter reports the bear's jaw as OG_PART.weapon. Nothing in src or tests records that.
